mechanism: A records vault cut away so two routes are visible at once: a front route and an export route, both ending at the tray that holds invoice A-17 (owned by tenant A). Each route has a harness probe station with one rod per tenant and a result lamp per rod. The first control moves the ownership check between a gate on the front route (where the repair put it) and a guard collar at the invoice itself. The second control runs four probes. Refused rods stay pressed against whatever stopped them; rods that receive the invoice retract carrying a copy, amber when it was not expected.
spatialBenefit: Coverage here is route topology. From any angle the learner can see that the export corridor joins the tray beside the front gate rather than through it, watch B’s export rod pass the place where the gate is not, and compare the stopping points (gate versus shutter at the invoice) and returned copies after each placement.
beyondVideoTest: The learner chooses where the check sits and inspects the access paths and final contacts; the outcome (which probe fails, where each refused rod stops) follows from that spatial choice. The existing video shows one route’s fail/repair/rerun sequence and cannot show a bypass.

picks: Lamp or probe → tenant, route, expected and actual status, or stale/not run

interaction.initialState: Still; check on the front route; rods retracted; lamps dark.

expectedObservations: Check on the front route: A receives copies on both routes; B front rod stops flush on the gate bar; B export rod reaches the tray and returns an amber copy; lamps pass, pass, pass, amber. Caption notes a front-only harness would have reported green.
Moving the check: gate or guard swaps, rods clear, all four lamps turn stale grey, run label asks for a rerun.
Check at the invoice: A rods pass through open slots and return copies; both B rods stop flush on shutters at the invoice; all lamps pass; caption limits the claim to two routes and one invoice.

mapping.probes A and B: the allowed and forbidden cases the harness runs (200 and the example 403 policy)
mapping.front and export routes: two code paths that read the same invoice
mapping.gate / guard: where the per-resource ownership predicate runs (one handler versus the shared lookup)
mapping.stale lamps: “yesterday’s green result is not evidence for today’s patch”

limitations: Physical metaphor: the gate and guard stand for an ownership predicate in code, not for separate tenant storage; per-tenant lanes stand for requests, not network paths. 403 is the guide’s example policy.
The four probes are themselves narrow; the caption says other routes and records remain untested, but the scene does not show adding a probe.
Does not show weakening an assertion or required status checks.
